old: 随机客流和路况变化使公交车头时距失衡，增加串车风险和乘客等待时间。驻站可调节车辆离站时刻，但受到车辆与站点差异、环境条件及动作上限的制约。强化学习可依据状态选择动作，却难以在实际运营中反复试错，最终策略又面临训练与使用环境的分布偏移，使其现实部署面临困难。本文围绕从仿真到现实的驻站控制，先研究未预先获得目标域训练数据时的平稳随机鲁棒学习与非平稳随机适应学习，再研究获得目标域离线数据后的跨保真训练及模型修正。
new: 客流到达与道路运行时间的随机波动容易造成公交车头时距失衡，增加串车风险和乘客等待时间。驻站控制通过主动延迟车辆离站调节相邻车辆间隔，但其效果受到车辆状态、运行条件和允许驻站时长的制约。针对实际公交运营中训练交互受限，以及仿真训练与目标环境之间存在分布差异的问题，本文围绕共享策略的鲁棒学习、非平稳运行中的条件响应、目标离线数据支持的跨保真训练和世界模型修正开展研究。
reason: 从交通问题引入四项研究，减少信息条件的重复。

old: （1）针对不同车辆与站点的差异及随机运行中的动作价值估计波动，提出结合类别特征嵌入与连续状态的共享驻站策略，并提出鲁棒集成软演员评论家方法（Robust Ensemble Soft Actor-Critic，RE-SAC）。以候车时间的两倍与车内时间之和作为广义乘客时间，在学习器及训练设置一致的类别表征比较中，学习嵌入相对独热编码在正常运行、客流激增和快速切换下，分别降低5.51%、1.41%和4.91%的人均广义乘客时间。单一驻站动作、车头时距目标下，RE-SAC相对主流对照在所测随机环境中具有更低的计划时距偏差和更稳定的价值评价。结果表明，在高不确定性环境中，引入保守偏移以提高价值评价稳定性，可以带来更好的控制效果；但不同运营目标仍存在取舍。

old: Random passenger demand and changing road traffic disrupt bus headways, promote bunching, and increase passenger waiting time. Holding control regulates departure times, but its effectiveness depends on vehicle and stop characteristics, operating conditions, and the maximum permitted holding time. Reinforcement learning can select actions from operational observations, yet repeated trial-and-error learning on an operating fleet is impractical, and the resulting policy may encounter a distribution shift between training and deployment environments. This thesis studies sim-to-real bus holding control: robust learning under stationary stochastic conditions and adaptive learning under non-stationary stochastic conditions first address settings without pre-collected target-domain training data; cross-fidelity learning and model correction then incorporate target-domain offline data.
new: Random passenger arrivals and travel-time fluctuations disrupt bus headways, promote bunching, and increase passenger waiting time. Holding control regulates headways by delaying departures, but its effectiveness depends on vehicle states, operating conditions, and the permitted holding duration. To address limited opportunities for training interaction in real bus operations and distribution differences between simulation and target environments, this thesis studies robust shared-policy learning, conditional responses to non-stationary operations, cross-fidelity training supported by target offline data, and world-model correction.
reason: 与修改后中文摘要开头对应。

old: To address differences among vehicles and stops and fluctuations in action-value estimates during stochastic operations, this thesis proposes a shared holding policy combining categorical feature embeddings with continuous observations and develops Robust Ensemble Soft Actor-Critic (RE-SAC). Generalized passenger time is defined as twice waiting time plus onboard time. With the same learner and training settings, learned embeddings reduce generalized passenger time relative to one-hot encoding by 5.51%, 1.41%, and 4.91% under routine operations, demand surges, and rapid switching. With a single holding action and a headway objective, RE-SAC achieves lower planned-headway deviation and more stable value evaluation than the tested mainstream baselines. These results show that introducing a conservative bias to stabilize value evaluation can improve control under high uncertainty, while different operating objectives retain tradeoffs.
new: To address vehicle and stop differences and fluctuating action-value estimates, this thesis constructs a shared holding policy combining categorical embeddings with continuous states and develops Robust Ensemble Soft Actor-Critic (RE-SAC). Ensemble value estimates, target shifts, and disagreement penalties regulate policy updates. Generalized passenger time is defined as twice waiting time plus onboard time. With the same learner and training settings, learned embeddings reduce generalized passenger time relative to one-hot encoding by 5.51%, 1.41%, and 4.91% under routine operations, demand surges, and rapid switching, respectively. In the multi-line experiment with a headway objective, RE-SAC reduces planned-headway deviation and forward-backward headway imbalance relative to SAC by 5.00 and 7.36 seconds, respectively. The results show that categorical information and conservative value evaluation can improve holding control under the tested conditions, while gains in headway regularity and passenger time depend on the training objective.
reason: 与中文第1项对应，保留具体参照和单位。

old: To address changing operating laws and the limited ability of holding to alter departure times, this thesis proposes Bayesian Adaptive Policy Regularization (BAPR), using environment identification and operating-mode confidence adjustment, and subsequently develops Causal-Symbolic Bayesian Adaptive Policy Regularization (CS-BAPR). Across routine demand, single and repeated environmental changes, sustained high demand, and brief extreme demand, training stabilization reduces the mean headway-reward penalty relative to the preceding BAPR configuration by 58.82% to 69.79% with a single holding action. Matched comparisons with RE-SAC support stronger conditional adaptation when operating laws change, while structured policy outputs do not provide an additional benefit in every condition. Under a passenger-time objective, service-cost differences narrow, so headway gains cannot be interpreted as equal reductions in passenger time.
new: To address changes in passenger demand and operating dynamics, this thesis studies confidence adjustment in Bayesian Adaptive Policy Regularization (BAPR) and develops Causal-Symbolic Bayesian Adaptive Policy Regularization (CS-BAPR). The bus implementation adjusts conservatism using recent operating information during training and combines training stabilization with policy output structures to evaluate fixed-policy responses to changing conditions. Across six conditions covering routine demand, single and repeated changes, sustained high demand, and brief extreme demand, the stabilized multilayer-perceptron configuration reduces the mean headway-reward penalty by 58.82% to 69.79% and absolute planned-headway deviation by 27.10% to 36.55% relative to the preceding BAPR configuration. The additional benefit of arithmetic outputs varies across conditions. With a passenger-time objective, the stabilized configuration increases generalized passenger time by 0.068% to 0.268%. Its main improvement therefore concerns headway control.

old: To reduce dependence on repeated trial-and-error data collection in the target operating environment, this thesis develops a bus-specific cross-fidelity workflow based on Hybrid Offline-and-Online Reinforcement Learning (H2O) and the Improved Framework for Hybrid Offline-and-Online Reinforcement Learning with Dynamics Gaps (H2O+). Fixed SUMO offline data and simplified-simulator interaction jointly support policy training. Simultaneous-arrival encoding, a single action that adds either no extra holding or a positive holding duration, and a completion reserve for late-operation states with low onboard loads and insufficient following service form the complete controller. In 1,350 paired evaluations covering 10 new environment blocks, three demand levels, and nine controllers, the reserve reduces within-window generalized passenger time by 92.12 seconds, or 3.71%, and increases completion by 0.466 percentage points relative to the direct parent with the same learned policy. An update-budget-matched comparison supports hybrid training over the tested offline-only scheme.
new: To reduce dependence on repeated trial-and-error data collection in the target environment, this thesis develops a bus-specific cross-fidelity workflow based on Hybrid Offline-and-Online Reinforcement Learning (H2O) and the Improved Framework for Hybrid Offline-and-Online Reinforcement Learning with Dynamics Gaps (H2O+). Fixed SUMO offline data are combined with simplified-simulator interaction. The workflow uses structured encoding of simultaneous arrivals and a mixed action representation for zero or positive holding, together with a trip-completion safeguard for low-load states without an active following vehicle within a specified service window. In 1,350 paired evaluations covering 10 new environment blocks, three demand levels, and nine controllers, the safeguard reduces within-window generalized passenger time by 92.12 seconds, or 3.71%, and increases completion by 0.466 percentage points relative to the same learned policy without this safeguard. With matched update budgets, hybrid training reduces generalized passenger time relative to offline-only training by 16.66 and 19.75 seconds under routine and 1.25-fold demand, respectively.

old: To address source-target transition mismatch, this thesis proposes the Model-Corrected World Model (MC-WM), selecting residual correction or direct target modeling using held-out prediction errors and weighting one-step model samples through log-confidence evaluation. The bus extension uses fixed target offline data and hybrid event models, with a normalized confidence backup limiting attenuation of model updates. With a single holding action and a passenger-time objective, generalized passenger time decreases relative to a Daganzo-style rule with the same completion reserve by 57.67, 70.67, and 76.26 seconds under calibrated, joint 50%, and joint 75% source-parameter mismatch, respectively. Joint mismatch changes road speeds, passenger OD demand, intersection delays, and required stopping-service times together. With a headway objective, MC-WM also improves over H2O+ under large source mismatch. These results support using target offline data to correct source-simulator training for both operating objectives.
new: To address source-target transition mismatch, this thesis proposes the Model-Corrected World Model (MC-WM). Held-out target data are used to compare residual correction with direct target modeling, and log-confidence evaluation weights one-step predicted samples for value updates. The bus extension combines hybrid event prediction with a normalized confidence backup to limit attenuation of the model contribution during training. In experiments with a passenger-time objective and 20 independent initializations, a fixed model-loss coefficient of 0.25 reduces generalized passenger time relative to the hybrid-learning baseline without a world model by 51.14, 69.93, and 87.05 seconds under calibrated, joint 50%, and joint 75% source-parameter mismatch, respectively, with equal weighting of test conditions. The reductions mainly arise from shorter waiting times. Supplementary experiments trained with a headway reward also report passenger-service outcomes, using different training repetitions and model coefficients. The results show that target-data-supported model correction can improve bus holding training under the tested source-parameter mismatches.

old: The thesis connects stationary robust control, non-stationary adaptation, cross-fidelity transfer, and world-model correction through target-domain data availability. Its central mechanism combines records from a detailed simulator with interaction in a simplified simulator to learn holding policies that generalize to unseen SUMO scenarios. The results support replacing SUMO offline data with real bus-operation records and continuing training in an interactive simulator as a pathway from simulation toward real bus holding control.
new: The thesis develops bus holding methods that address stochastic operations, changing operating conditions, target-data use, and prediction correction. Detailed-simulator records and simplified-simulator interaction support policy training, while unseen SUMO scenarios evaluate generalization. This workflow provides a basis for future studies using real bus-operation records together with interactive simulation.

old: 学习方法同时增加了训练数据和评价条件的重要性。公交车辆不是始终同步行动的固定对象，其决策往往由到站、完成服务或实际发车事件触发；不同站点、班次和时段产生的样本也不均衡。有限训练数据上的策略改善，需要进一步接受新需求、新路况和新运行日的检验。为应对这些问题，本论文从类别状态与共享策略出发，逐步研究价值估计稳定性、非平稳运行适应及目标数据支持的迁移。
new: 学习策略的性能不仅取决于算法设计，还取决于训练数据的覆盖范围和评价场景的设置。公交车辆的决策通常由到站、完成服务或实际发车事件触发，不同站点、班次和时段产生的样本量也不均衡。因此，需要在共享运行经验的同时保留车辆与站点差异，并在新需求、新路况和新运行日中检验策略。本文据此从类别状态与共享策略出发，逐步研究价值估计稳定性、非平稳运行中的条件响应，以及目标数据支持的迁移。
